Choose how the isolation will be executed:
- 'Full' -> complete isolation of polygons
- 'Ext' -> will isolate only on the outside
- 'Int' -> will isolate only on the inside
'Exterior' isolation is almost always possible
(with the right tool) but 'Interior'
isolation can be done only when there is an opening
inside of the polygon (e.g polygon is a 'doughnut' shape).

How much (percentage) of the tool width to overlap each tool pass.
Adjust the value starting with lower values
and increasing it if areas that should be processed are still 
not processed.
Lower values = faster processing, faster execution on CNC.
Higher values = slow processing and slow execution on CNC
due of too many paths.

Distance by which to avoid
the edges of the polygon to
be painted.

Algorithm for painting:
- Standard: Fixed step inwards.
- Seed-based: Outwards from seed.
- Line-based: Parallel lines.
- Laser-lines: Active only for Gerber objects.
Will create lines that follow the traces.
- Combo: In case of failure a new method will be picked from the above
in the order specified.

Draw lines between resulting
segments to minimize tool lifts.

Cut around the perimeter of the polygon
to trim rough edges.

The 'Operation' can be:
- Isolation -> will ensure that the non-copper clearing is always complete.
If it's not successful then the non-copper clearing will fail, too.
- Clear -> the regular non-copper clearing.

Margin over bounds. A positive value here
will make the cutout of the PCB further from
the actual PCB border

The size of the bridge gaps in the cutout
used to keep the board connected to
the surrounding material (the one 
from which the PCB is cutout).

The type of gap:
- Bridge -> the cutout will be interrupted by bridges
- Thin -> same as 'bridge' but it will be thinner by partially milling the gap
- M-Bites -> 'Mouse Bites' - same as 'bridge' but covered with drill holes

The depth until the milling is done
in order to thin the gaps.
The drill hole diameter when doing mouse bites.
The spacing between drill holes when doing mouse bites.

Create a convex shape surrounding the entire PCB.
Used only if the source object type is Gerber.

Number of gaps used for the Automatic cutout.
There can be maximum 8 bridges/gaps.
The choices are:
- None  - no gaps
- lr    - left + right
- tb    - top + bottom
- 4     - left + right +top + bottom
- 2lr   - 2*left + 2*right
- 2tb  - 2*top + 2*bottom
- 8     - 2*left + 2*right +2*top + 2*bottom

Drill depth (negative)
below the copper surface.

Some drill bits (the larger ones) need to drill deeper
to create the desired exit hole diameter due of the tip shape.
The value here can compensate the Cut Z parameter.

Use multiple passes to limit
the cut depth in each pass. Will
cut multiple times until Cut Z is
reached.

DPP. Depth per Pass.
The value used to cut into material on each pass.
Depth of each pass (positive).

Tool height when travelling
across the XY plane.

Tool speed while drilling
(in units per minute).
So called 'Plunge' feedrate.
This is for linear move G01.

Tool speed while drilling
(in units per minute).
This is for the rapid move G00.
It is useful only for Marlin,
ignore for any other cases.

Speed of the spindle
in RPM (optional)

Dwell.
Check this if a delay is needed to allow
the spindle motor to reach its set speed.

Dwell Time.
A delay used to allow the motor spindle reach its set speed.
If the selected tool has slots then they will be drilled.
How much (percentage) of the tool diameter to overlap previous drill hole.

If the slot length is not completely covered by drill holes,
add a drill hole on the slot end point.

Tool Shape. 
Can be:
C1 ... C4 = circular tool with x flutes
B = ball tip milling tool
V = v-shape milling tool

V-Dia.
Diameter of the tip for V-Shape Tools.

V-Agle.
Angle at the tip for the V-Shape Tools.

Tool Type.
Can be:
Iso = isolation cut
Rough = rough cut, low feedrate, multiple passes
Finish = finishing cut, high feedrate

Tool Offset.
Can be of a few types:
Path = zero offset
In = offset inside by half of tool diameter
Out = offset outside by half of tool diameter
Custom = custom offset using the Custom Offset value

Custom Offset.
A value to be used as offset from the current path.

Cutting Depth.
The depth at which to cut into material.

Multi Depth.
Selecting this will allow cutting in multiple passes,
each pass adding a DPP parameter depth.

DPP. Depth per Pass.
The value used to cut into material on each pass.

Clearance Height.
Height at which the milling bit will travel between cuts,
above the surface of the material, avoiding all fixtures.

Extra Cut.
If checked, after a isolation is finished an extra cut
will be added where the start and end of isolation meet
such as that this point is covered by this extra cut to
ensure a complete isolation.

Extra Cut length.
If checked, after a isolation is finished an extra cut
will be added where the start and end of isolation meet
such as that this point is covered by this extra cut to
ensure a complete isolation. This is the length of
the extra cut.

Feedrate X-Y. Feedrate
The speed on XY plane used while cutting into material.

Feedrate Z
The speed on Z plane.

FR Rapids. Feedrate Rapids
Speed used while moving as fast as possible.
This is used only by some devices that can't use
the G0 g-code command. Mostly 3D printers.

Spindle Speed.
If it's left empty it will not be used.
The speed of the spindle in RPM.

Dwell.
Check this if a delay is needed to allow
the spindle motor to reach its set speed.

Dwell Time.
A delay used to allow the motor spindle reach its set speed.
